title: No SLA or deadline visible on review items in reviewer queue — `MyReviewsTab` shows title/status/assigned date only; no due date, no overdue flag; reviewer with 30 items has no urgency prioritisation; violates ISO 19011:2018 §5.5
description: Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/MyReviewsTab.jsx Root Cause: `MyReviewsTab` shows title, status, and assigned date only. No due date, no overdue flag, no SLA indicator. A reviewer with 30 items has no urgency basis for prioritisation. Claude Fix Prompt: Add SLA column: `{review.dueDate ? ({isPast(review.dueDate) ? 'OVERDUE' : \`Due in \${differenceInDays(review.dueDate, new Date())}d\`}) : No deadline}`. Sort queue by `dueDate` ascending by default.

title: No per-access audit trail of who accessed a share link — `ShareLinkModal` shows `viewCount` only; no timestamp, recipient identifier, or IP per access event; violates ISO 27001:2022 Annex A 5.14
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/ShareLinkModal.jsx Root Cause: Share link modal shows `viewCount` total only. No per-access record with timestamp, IP address, or recipient identifier is stored or displayed. Claude Fix Prompt: Backend: on every share link access, append to `ShareLinkAccessLog`: `{linkId, accessedAt: new Date(), ipAddress: req.ip, userAgent: req.headers['user-agent']}`. Frontend `ShareLinkModal`: add `View access log ({accessLog.length} entries){accessLog.map(e =>
{formatDateTime(e.accessedAt)} — {e.ipAddress}
)}`.

title: Share URL constructed client-side using `window.location.origin` — URL varies by environment (staging vs. production, SSO proxy); links emailed to partners could be broken in production if constructed on staging
description: Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/ShareLinkModal.jsx Root Cause: Share URL built as `window.location.origin + '/share/' + linkToken`. If the modal is opened on a staging or preview environment, the emailed link points to staging, not production. Claude Fix Prompt: Source the base URL from environment variable: `const shareUrl = \`\${process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/share/\${linkToken}\`;`. Ensure `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` is set to the canonical production URL in all deployment environments. Render a preview of the constructed URL before sending: `{shareUrl}`.

title: Expiry alert thresholds hardcoded at 7/14/30/60 days — all organisations use the same tiers; large enterprises needing 180-day warnings cannot adjust; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/ExpiryDashboard.jsx, trust-vault-service/src/jobs/expiryCheck.ts

Root Cause: Expiry alert thresholds hardcoded in both the dashboard filter chips and the cron job. Organisations needing 90-day or 180-day advance warnings (common in enterprise) cannot configure this.

Claude Fix Prompt: Add org-level setting `expiryAlertThresholds: number[]` (default `[7, 14, 30, 60]`). In `expiryCheck.ts`: `const thresholds = org.settings.expiryAlertThresholds || [7, 14, 30, 60]; const certs = await CertService.getExpiringSoon(Math.max(...thresholds));`. In `ExpiryDashboard`, render filter chips from the org setting rather than hardcoded values.

title: No automated escalation or notification when certifications cross expiry thresholds — `ExpiryDashboard` is monitoring-only; no push notification, no workflow action triggered; organisations not checking daily could miss threshold crossings; violates Annex A 5.33
description:
Files: trust-vault-service/src/jobs/expiryCheck.ts

Root Cause: `ExpiryDashboard` is monitoring-only — it displays expiry status but triggers no push notifications, emails, or workflow actions when a threshold is crossed.

Claude Fix Prompt: In `expiryCheck.ts` cron job, after identifying threshold crossings: `await NotificationService.send({ userId: cert.ownerId, type: 'cert_expiry_warning', title: \`Certification expiring in \${daysLeft} days\`, body: \`\${cert.name} expires on \${formatDate(cert.expiryDate)}\`, link: \`/trust-vault/certifications/\${cert._id}\` });`. Record `lastNotifiedAt` to prevent duplicate sends.

title: Expiry look-ahead window fixed at 90 days — `getExpiringSoon(90)` hardcoded; certifications expiring in 91+ days invisible; organisations planning 6-month renewals have no visibility
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/ExpiryDashboard.jsx

Root Cause: `getExpiringSoon(90)` hardcoded. Certifications expiring in 91+ days are completely invisible in the dashboard even when organisations plan 6-month renewals.

Claude Fix Prompt: Replace hardcoded `90` with a configurable look-ahead: `const lookAhead = org.settings.expiryLookAheadDays || 90; getExpiringSoon(lookAhead)`. Add a date-range picker in the dashboard header: `<Select value={lookAhead} onValueChange={setLookAhead}><SelectItem value={30}>Next 30 days</SelectItem><SelectItem value={90}>Next 90 days</SelectItem><SelectItem value={180}>Next 180 days</SelectItem></Select>`.

title: `redactedSummary` error-prefix guard is a data corruption symptom not a fix — `TrustNetworkSharingPanel` guards `startsWith('Error')`/`startsWith('Axios')` indicating error strings persisted to DB as content; root cause in API error handler not fixed; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.3
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/TrustNetworkSharingPanel.jsx

Root Cause: Guard `startsWith('Error')` / `startsWith('Axios')` in the display logic indicates that API error strings are being persisted to the database as `redactedSummary` content. The root cause in the API error handler is unfixed.

Claude Fix Prompt: Fix the root cause in the Trust Vault API: wrap the `redactedSummary` generation endpoint in proper error handling — `try { const summary = await generateRedactedSummary(cert); return res.json({summary}); } catch (err) { logger.error('redactedSummary generation failed', err); return res.status(500).json({error: 'Summary generation failed'}); }`. Never persist an error string to `redactedSummary`. Remove the client-side guard once fixed.

title: No per-partner access log for Trust Network sharing — `TrustNetworkSharingPanel` shows `allowedPartnerIds` list only; no record of when each partner last accessed or how many times they downloaded; violates ISO 27001:2022 Annex A 5.14
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/TrustNetworkSharingPanel.jsx

Root Cause: Panel shows only `allowedPartnerIds` list. No record of when each partner last accessed the shared certification or how many times they downloaded it.

Claude Fix Prompt: Backend: log `{partnerId, certId, accessedAt, action: 'view'|'download'}` on each Trust Network access. Frontend `TrustNetworkSharingPanel`: add `<AccessLogTable partnerId={p.id} certId={certId} />` expandable per partner row showing their access history.

title: Draft certifications can be mapped to compliance frameworks before validation — `CertFrameworkMappingPanel` available regardless of cert status; draft certs contribute to framework coverage score; inflates coverage metrics with unvalidated evidence; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.2
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/CertFrameworkMappingPanel.jsx

Root Cause: `CertFrameworkMappingPanel` renders and accepts mappings regardless of certification `status`. Draft certificates contribute to framework coverage scores before any validation has occurred.

Claude Fix Prompt: In `CertFrameworkMappingPanel`: `if (cert.status === 'draft') return (<Alert>Framework mapping is only available for validated certifications. Complete the review process first.</Alert>);`. Backend framework mapping creation endpoint: `if (cert.status === 'draft') return res.status(400).json({error: 'Cannot map draft certifications to frameworks'});`.

title: Partial-scope certification mappings not disclosed to partners or in public share views — partner may assume full ISO 27001 coverage when only 5 specific controls are covered; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.1
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/TrustNetworkSharingPanel.jsx

Root Cause: When a certification covers only a partial scope (e.g., 5 specific Annex A controls rather than the full standard), this limitation is not surfaced to partners in the Trust Network shared view or share link view.

Claude Fix Prompt: In the shared certification view: `{cert.scope === 'partial' && <Alert variant="warning"><AlertTitle>Partial Scope</AlertTitle>This certification covers: {cert.scopeDescription}. It does not represent full compliance with {cert.framework}.</Alert>}`. Add `scope` and `scopeDescription` fields to the certification schema if not already present.

title: No cryptographic hash or tamper-evident seal per certification version — `VersionHistory` shows version/changeType/changedBy/timestamp only; no SHA-256 hash stored or displayed; chain-of-custody cannot be verified; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5.3
description: Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/VersionHistory.jsx, trust-vault-service/src/services/CertificationService.ts Root Cause: `VersionHistory` shows version number, change type, changed by, and timestamp only. No SHA-256 hash of the document content is computed on upload or stored/displayed per version. Claude Fix Prompt: Backend `CertificationService.createVersion`: `const hash = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(versionContent)).digest('hex'); version.contentHash = hash;`. Frontend `VersionHistory`: `{version.contentHash?.slice(0, 16)}…` with copy-to-clipboard button. Add `Copy full hash` link for audit packages.

title: Three parallel workflow state maps inconsistent across components — `CERT_TRANSITIONS`, `CERT_STATUS_ACTIONS`, `STATUS_CONFIG` define lifecycle in three separate places with divergences; future changes risk further inconsistency; violates ISO 27001:2022 Clause 7.5
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/WorkflowActionPanel.jsx

Root Cause: `CERT_TRANSITIONS`, `CERT_STATUS_ACTIONS`, and `STATUS_CONFIG` each define parts of the certification lifecycle independently and have diverged (TV-004 is one consequence). Any future lifecycle change risks further inconsistency.

Claude Fix Prompt: Create a single source of truth: `CERTIFICATION_LIFECYCLE` object: `{ draft: { label: 'Draft', color: 'gray', actions: ['submit_for_review'] }, under_review: { ... }, active: { ... }, expiring_soon: { ... }, expired: { ... }, revoked: { ... } }`. Derive all three current maps from this single config at module load time.

title: Audit log event coverage undocumented and completeness unverifiable — `CertificationDetails` shows audit log but no documentation of which events are captured; auditor cannot verify completeness of evidence trail; violates ISO 27001:2022 Annex A 8.15
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/CertificationDetails.jsx

Root Cause: `CertificationDetails` displays an audit log but provides no documentation of which events are captured, which actors can generate them, or whether the log is complete. An auditor cannot verify the trail is exhaustive.

Claude Fix Prompt: Add an info tooltip on the audit log heading: `<Tooltip content="Events captured: view, status_transition, reviewer_assigned, reviewer_submitted, note_added, framework_mapped, framework_archived, share_link_created, trust_network_enabled. Document downloads logged separately in access log."><InfoIcon /></Tooltip>`. Ensure all events listed in the tooltip are actually emitted in the backend.

title: ISO 27001 version (2013 vs 2022) never shown — `FRAMEWORK_COLORS = { 'ISO27001': 'blue' }` single entry; all ISO 27001 certs appear identical; mandatory 2013→2022 transition deadline passed; auditor cannot verify edition compliance; violates Clause 7.5.1
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/constants.js

Root Cause: `FRAMEWORK_COLORS = { 'ISO27001': 'blue' }` — single entry treating all ISO 27001 certifications as equivalent. The mandatory 2013→2022 transition deadline has passed and editions are architecturally different.

Claude Fix Prompt: Expand to: `FRAMEWORK_COLORS = { 'ISO27001:2013': 'blue', 'ISO27001:2022': 'indigo', 'ISO27001': 'blue' }`. Update certification schema to store `frameworkVersion: '2013' | '2022'`. Display badge in certification cards: `<Badge>{cert.framework} {cert.frameworkVersion}</Badge>`. Flag 2013 certs with a deprecation warning.

title: Entire Trust Vault gated on single permission — no sub-feature RBAC; `WorkflowActionPanel` does not filter by role; any `trust_vault.write` user can revoke; four-eyes principle unenforceable; violates ISO 27001:2022 Annex A 5.3
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/WorkflowActionPanel.jsx

Root Cause: All Trust Vault features sit behind a single `trust_vault.write` permission. `WorkflowActionPanel` does not differentiate by action type — any `trust_vault.write` user can revoke certifications.

Claude Fix Prompt: Add sub-permissions: `trust_vault.review` (submit reviews), `trust_vault.approve` (close/approve), `trust_vault.revoke` (revoke). In `WorkflowActionPanel`: `if (action.targetState === 'revoked' && !hasPermission('trust_vault.revoke')) return null;`. Backend: enforce sub-permissions on transition endpoints.

title: Vault Health grade formula undisclosed — `VaultHealthWidget` shows score and A–F grade with no tooltip, methodology explanation, or sub-dimension weighting; management review cannot cite unexplained automated grade; violates ISO/IEC 27007 §6.4.9
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/VaultHealthWidget.jsx

Root Cause: `VaultHealthWidget` shows a score (e.g., 73) and an A–F grade with no tooltip, methodology explanation, or sub-dimension weighting. Management review cannot cite an unexplained automated grade.

Claude Fix Prompt: Add methodology tooltip: `<Tooltip content="Vault Health = (Active Certs 40%) + (No Expiring Soon 25%) + (All Reviews Complete 20%) + (Trust Network Active 15%). Grade: A=90+, B=75+, C=60+, D=45+, F=<45"><InfoIcon className="w-4 h-4 inline ml-1 text-muted-foreground" /></Tooltip>`. Link to a "How is this calculated?" documentation page.

title: No incident severity escalation path — `IncidentForm` severity field has no SLA timer or automated escalation when `severity = 'critical'` remains `status = 'open'` beyond threshold; critical incident open 72h looks identical to one created 5 minutes ago; violates Annex A 5.26
description:
Files: vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/trust-vault/IncidentForm.jsx, trust-vault-service/

Root Cause: `severity` field has no SLA timer or automated escalation when a critical severity incident remains `status: 'open'` beyond a threshold (e.g., 72 hours). A critical incident looks identical to one created 5 minutes ago.

Claude Fix Prompt: Backend job: `IncidentEscalationJob` — daily query for `{severity: 'critical', status: {$in: ['open','investigating']}, createdAt: {$lt: subHours(new Date(), 72)}}`. For each: send escalation notification to CISO/security lead role. Update `escalatedAt`. Frontend: display SLA countdown on critical open incidents: `<Badge variant="destructive">SLA: {hoursRemaining}h remaining</Badge>`.
